questions.q: The transformer winding that is connected to the source is called the “_____” winding and the transformer winding that is connected to the load is called the “_____” winding.
Both the primary and secondary windings are wound on the same iron core, so the electromagnetic field from the primary winding cuts the secondary winding, which induces a voltage on the _____.
The _____ on the secondary winding is a function of the number of secondary wire loops cut by the primary electromagnetic field.
The relationship of the number of turns of wire on the _____ as compared to the number of turns on the _____ is called the transformer “winding turns ratio.”
A transformer has a primary winding of twenty turns and a secondary of ten turns. The winding turns ratio of this transformer is _____.
The relationship between primary voltage and secondary voltage is called the transformer “_____ turns ratio.”
If the primary phase voltage is 480V and the secondary phase voltage is 240V, the voltage turns ratio is _____.
The secondary voltage of a 5:1 transformer is _____ if the primary is 240V.
The secondary voltage of a 4:1 turns ratio transformer is _____ if the primary is 240V.

If the primary and secondary windings of a transformer have the same number of wire loops (turns), the secondary output voltage will be the same as the primary input voltage. This type of transformer is called a(an) “_____ transformer.”
Autotransformers use a _____ winding for both the primary and secondary and are often referred to as “buck-boost transformers.”
Transformers are rated in _____.

The primary electromagnetic field induces a voltage in the secondary. As the secondary current flows, it produces an electromagnetic field that reduces the strength of the primary flux lines. This results in an increase in _____ current.

Current flow in a secondary transformer winding creates an electromagnetic field that opposes the primary electromagnetic field resulting in less primary CEMF. The primary current automatically increases in direct proportion to the _____ current.
What is the secondary current for a fully loaded single-phase, 25 kVA, 480V to 240V transformer?
What is the secondary current for a fully loaded three-phase, 75 kVA, 480V to 208Y/120V transformer?
The secondary current for a fully loaded single-phase, 37.50 kVA, 480V to 240V transformer is _____.
What is the primary current for a fully loaded single-phase, 25 kVA, 480V to 240V transformer?
What is the primary current for a fully loaded three-phase, 75 kVA, 480V to 208Y/120V transformer?
The primary current for a fully loaded three-phase, 37.50 kVA, 480V to 208Y/120V transformer is _____.
_____transformers contain a primary and a secondary mounted on a single laminated iron core.
_____transformers are constructed of three sets of single-phase windings that are connected together to create a three-phase system.
The _____ windings of a three-phase delta/wye-connected transformer are connected end-to-end with each other.
The _____ windings of a three-phase delta/wye-configured transformer have one end of each winding connected to a common point.
The voltage between any two primary wires is called “primary _____ voltage,” while the voltage between any two secondary wires is called “secondary _____ voltage.”
_____ voltage is the voltage between a phase wire and a neutral wire.
The _____ circuit wires are connected to each point where the winding leads meet.
The load wires are connected to each point where the _____ winding leads meet.
The voltage between any two primary wires is known as the “_____ line-to-line voltage,” while the voltage between any two secondary wires is referred to as the “_____ line-to-line voltage.”

The line-to-neutral voltage is the voltage between a phase wire and the neutral wire. In a delta/delta high-leg 4-wire system, the Line1- and Line 3-to-neutral voltage is 120V, and the Line2-to-neutral will be _____.
Overcurrent is current in excess of the equipment ampere rating or ampacity of the wires. It may result from a(an) _____.
A(An)_____ is the operation of equipment or wires in excess of their rated ampacity.
A(An) _____ is an electrical connection between any two phase wires, or a phase wire and neutral wire.
A(An) _____ occurs when an unintentional electrical connection occurs between a phase wire and metal parts of enclosures, raceways, and/or equipment.
Overcurrent protection is typically provided by _____.
Fuses consist of a _____ element connected to end blades or caps, surrounded by silica sand filler material enclosed in a tube.
When a sustained overload occurs through the element(s) of a fuse, the heat melts _____, stopping the flow of current.
questions.matched: key says “a segment of the element” (later printing wording for choice c)

questions.q: When a short circuit or ground fault occurs through the element of a fuse, the heat in the element rises to a point where _____ in the fuse melt to stop electrical current flow.

choices.b: a small portion of the segment

questions.matched: key says “multiple segments” (later printing wording for choice a)

questions.q: A _____ fuse is referred to as a nontime-delay fuse and is the least expensive type.
A _____ fuse is often called a “time-delay fuse.”
A _____ fuse is designed to clear a short circuit or ground fault in less than one-half a cycle.
A _____ is capable of being opened and closed manually and automatically opens during an overcurrent condition.
_____circuit breakers operate on the principle that as the current increases, the time it takes for the device to open decreases.

The _____ trip element of a circuit breaker operates on the time-current principle of being inversely proportional to the magnitude of the current, which means that as the overload current increases, the time it takes for the trip element to open decreases.
Inverse time circuit breakers have a(an) _____ trip unit that responds to short-circuit and ground-fault currents.
_____ circuit breakers operate on the principle of electromagnetism only and are commonly known as motor circuit protectors.
_____ circuit breakers permit the thermal and electromagnetic trip current and/or time settings to be adjusted to provide the user with flexibility for specific applications.
The time it takes for an overcurrent protective device to open is plotted on a _____ curve chart.
As the overload current _____, the time it takes for the thermal trip element to open decreases.
To quickly clear a short circuit, the short-circuit _____ must rise to a level that is between ten and twenty times the rating of the circuit overcurrent protective device.
To quickly clear a(an) _____, the ground-fault current needs to rise to a level between ten and twenty times the rating of the circuit overcurrent protective device.

To remove dangerous touch voltage on metal parts produced by a ground fault, the fault-current path must have _____ to allow the fault current to quickly rise to facilitate the opening of the protection device.
Available short-circuit current is the _____ current in amperes that is available at a given point in the electrical system.
The available short-circuit current is highest at the utility transformer and lowest at the _____ load because of the impedance of the circuit.
The available short-circuit current is different at each point of the electrical system; it is highest at the _____.
The available short-circuit current at the _____ transformer is provided by the electric utility; no calculation is required.
The factor(s) that impact the available short-circuit current on the load side of a transformer is(are) _____.
What is the approximate available short-circuit current on the secondary of a 50 kVA, 480V to 240V transformer having an impedance rating of 1.20 percent?
What is the approximate available short-circuit current on the secondary of a three-phase, 112.50 kVA, 480V to 208Y/120V transformer having an impedance rating of 2.40 percent?
Circuit breakers and fuses are intended to interrupt the circuit, and they must have an ampere interrupting rating (AIR) _____ for the available short-circuit current.
If the protective device is not rated to _____ the available fault current at its listed voltage rating, it can explode while attempting to clear the fault.
Equipment must have a(an) _____ current rating that permits the protection device to clear a short circuit or ground fault without extensive damage to the equipment components.
If the equipment is not rated to _____ the available short-circuit current, it can explode while waiting for the circuit protective device to clear the fault.
“_____” of overcurrent protective devices is when the devices are designed to clear a short circuit or ground fault in a manner that localizes the short circuit or ground fault to that given circuit.
Selective coordination of overcurrent protective devices prevents _____ power losses to loads not part of the faulted circuit.
Lack of selective coordination of overcurrent protective devices can result in unintended _____ to loads not part of the faulted circuit.
GFCI protective devices detect the _____ current between circuit wires.
If the difference between the current leaving and returning through the current transformer of the GFCI protective device exceeds _____ (± 1 mA), the solid-state circuitry de-energizes the circuit.
A(An) _____ wire is not necessary for the proper function of a GFCI device.
GFCIs detect connections between the neutral wire and the metal parts of the electrical system (case). If a neutral connection to metal parts occurs, the GFCI protective device will _____.
Severe electric shock or death can occur if a person touches the _____ and neutral wires at the same time, even if the circuit is GFCI protected.
A hazard can exist if the electronics within a GFCI fail because the circuit remains _____ without GFCI protection.
GFCIs can only be properly tested by pressing the GFCI _____ button.
A special purpose GFCI device is used in circuits where the voltage-to-ground is greater than _____.
An arc-fault circuit interrupter is a device intended to de-energize a circuit when it detects the current waveform characteristics unique to a(an) _____ fault.
A _____ arcing fault can occur when the insulation between two wires degrades to a level where arcing can take place across the insulation between the two wires.

The current in an arcing fault is limited by the system impedance and the impedance of the arcing fault itself. Typically, at a receptacle, fault current will be above 75A, but not likely above _____.
A _____ arcing fault occurs when the wire within a cord is unintentionally broken, causing the current to arc across the gap in the wire.
_____ protective devices protect equipment by preventing damaging transient voltage from reaching the equipment.
_____ voltages inside a building can originate from high current loads that are switched on and off, such as those for copiers, laser printers, motors, and air-conditioning.
_____ sources of transient voltage include the switching of utility power factor correction capacitors or lightning strikes.
Surge protective devices are connected in _____ with the load.
The cross-sectional area of a wire is commonly expressed in _____.
In dc circuits, the only property that affects current flow is _____.
Wire dc resistance is determined by the _____.
Aluminum has _____ resistance to the flow of electrons than does copper.
Smaller wires have _____ resistance and larger wires have lower resistance.
The dc resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its _____.
The resistance of a wire is affected by temperature change. This is called the “_____.”
The _____ lists the resistance and area in circular mils for both direct-current and alternating-current circuit wires.

For ac circuits, the ac _____ of a wire is greater than the dc resistance because of eddy currents and skin effect.

_____currents are small independent currents that are produced as a result of the expanding and collapsing magnetic field. They flow erratically within the wire opposing current flow and consuming power.
Eddy currents are strongest in the center of the wires and repel the flowing electrons toward the wire surface. This is known as “_____ effect.”
The opposition to current flow is greater for alternating-current circuits than for direct-current circuits because of _____.
A _____ wire results in greater wire resistance and greater wire voltage drop.
Increased _____ flow will result in greater wire voltage drop.
A _____ circuit is a circuit consisting of two or more phase wires that have a voltage between them, and an equal voltage between each phase wire and the neutral wire.
The _____ wire is connected to the neutral point of a system and is intended to carry current under normal conditions.

The common point of a 4-wire, three-phase, wye-connected system; the midpoint of a 3-wire, single-phase system; or the midpoint of the single-phase portion of a three-phase, delta-connected system is referred to as the “_____ point.”

questions.q: Multiwire branch circuits are more _____ than 2-wire circuits in that they have fewer wires for a given number of circuits, which enables the use of a smaller raceway, and result in lower circuit voltage drop.

What is the circuit voltage drop over each line wire of a balanced 3-wire multiwire circuit? Each wire is 12 AWG, 150 ft long, supplying a 20A load.
Improper wiring or mishandling of multiwire circuits can cause _____.

choices.d: a fire hazard and/or equipment failure

The purpose of the NEC is for ______.

choices.a: it to be used as a design manual
choices.b: use as an instruction guide for untrained persons
choices.c: the practical safeguarding of persons and property

questions.q: Electrical hazards often occur because the initial ______ did not provide for increases in the use of electricity.
Compliance with the Code and proper maintenance result in an installation that is ______.

choices.c: not necessarily adequate for good service or future expansion

questions.q: Chapters 1, 2, 3, and 4 of the NEC apply ______.

choices.b: only to special occupancies and conditions
choices.c: only to special equipment and material

questions.q: Chapters 5, 6, and 7 of the NEC apply to ______ and may supplement or modify the requirements contained in Chapters 1 through 7.
The enforcement of the NEC is the responsibility of the authority having jurisdiction, who is responsible for ______.

By special permission, the authority having jurisdiction may waive specific NEC requirements or permit alternative methods where equivalent objectives can be achieved by establishing and maintaining effective _____.

If the Code requires new products that may not yet be available at the time the NEC is adopted, the ______ can allow products that comply with the most recent previous edition of the Code adopted by the jurisdiction.
In the NEC, the word(s) “______” indicate a mandatory requirement.
When the Code uses “______,” it indicates the actions are allowed but not required.

Article 100 contains only those definitions essential to the application of this Code. An article number in parentheses following the definition indicates that the definition only applies to that article.

Capable of being reached quickly for operation, renewal, or inspections without climbing over or under obstructions, removing obstacles, resorting to portable ladders, or the use of tools (other than keys) is known as “______.”
“______” means acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction.

A(An) ______ is a device, or group of devices, by which the conductors of a circuit can be disconnected from their source of supply.

questions.q: A location not normally subject to dampness or wetness but may be temporarily subject to dampness and wetness as in the case of a building under construction defines a ______ location.
A location unprotected and exposed to weather, subject to saturation, underground, or in concrete slabs in direct contact with the earth defines a ______ location.
For pools, fountains, and similar installations, the “low-voltage contact limit” is a voltage not exceeding ______.

choices.a: 15V (RMS) for sinusoidal ac or 21.20V peak for nonsinusoidal ac
choices.c: 12.40V peak for dc that is interrupted at a rate of 10 to 200 Hz

questions.q: A “luminaire” is a complete lighting unit consisting of a light source such as a lamp or lamps, together with the parts designed to position the ______ and connect it to the power supply.

The NEC defines a(an) “______” as one who has skills and knowledge related to the construction and operation of the electrical equipment and installations and has received safety training to recognize and avoid the hazards involved.
The conductors and equipment required or permitted by this Code shall be acceptable only if ______.
Equipment that is ______ or identified for a use shall be installed and used in accordance with any instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification.
The installation and use instructions for listed, labeled, or identified electrical equipment may be provided in the form of ______.

choices.c: an internet address to download instructions

questions.q: Unless identified for use in the operating environment, no conductors or equipment shall be ______ having a deteriorating effect on the conductors or equipment.

choices.a: located in damp or wet locations
choices.b: exposed to fumes, vapors, liquids, or gases

questions.q: Unused openings, other than those intended for the operation of equipment, those intended for mounting purposes, or permitted as part of the design for listed equipment shall be ______.

choices.a: filled with cable clamps or connectors only
choices.c: repaired only by welding or brazing in a metal slug
choices.d: closed to afford protection substantially equivalent to the wall of the equipment

questions.q: Internal parts of electrical equipment, including busbars, wiring terminals, insulators, and other surfaces, shall not be damaged or contaminated by foreign materials such as ______, or corrosive residues.

Tightening torque values for terminal connections shall be as indicated on equipment or in installation instructions provided by the manufacturer. An approved means shall be used to achieve the______ torque value.
Electrical equipment servicing and electrical preventive maintenance shall be performed by ______ trained in servicing and maintenance of equipment.
Each disconnecting means shall be legibly marked to indicate its purpose unless located and arranged so ______.

choices.a: that it can be locked out and tagged
choices.d: that it operates at less than 300 volts-to-ground

questions.q: Working space distances for enclosed live parts shall be measured from the ______ of equipment if the live parts are enclosed.
The minimum working space on a circuit for equipment operating at 120V to ground, with exposed live parts on one side and no live or grounded parts on the other side of the working space, is ______.
The minimum height of working spaces shall be clear and extend from the grade, floor, or platform to a height of ______ ft or the height of the equipment, whichever is greater.
The grade, floor, or platform in the required working space about electrical equipment shall be as level and flat as ______ for the entire required depth and width of the working space.

An insulated grounded conductor ______ or smaller shall be identified by a continuous white or gray outer finish, or by three continuous white or gray stripes along its entire length on other than green insulation.
At the time of installation, grounded conductors ______ or larger can be identified by a distinctive white or gray marking at their terminations.
Each multiwire branch circuit shall be provided with a means that will simultaneously disconnect all ______ conductors at the point where the branch circuit originates.
In dwelling unit kitchens, GFCI protection shall be provided for 125V through 250V receptacles ______.

choices.a: installed to serve the countertop surfaces
choices.b: installed to serve island or peninsula countertops
choices.c: installed to serve above or below the countertop surfaces

questions.q: In other than dwelling units, all 125V through 250V receptacles supplied by single-phase branch circuits rated 150 volts-to-ground or less, 50A or less, and three-phase branch circuits rated 100A or less, installed in(on) ______ shall have GFCI protection for personnel.
In other than dwelling units, GFCI protection is required for receptacles installed in ______.

choices.d: 6 ft Denotes change since first printing.

If a 20A branch circuit supplies multiple receptacles, the receptacles shall have an ampere rating of no less than _____.
The required heating, air-conditioning, and refrigeration equipment receptacle outlet shall be located _____ the equipment.

Surge-protective devices shall be installed in or adjacent to distribution equipment, connected to the _____ side of the feeder that contains branch circuit overcurrent protective device(s) that supply dwelling units, dormitory units, and guest rooms and suites.
Where a raceway enters a(an) _____ from outside, it shall be sealed in accordance with 300.5(G) and 300.7(A).

In accordance with Article 225—Outside Branch Circuits and Feeders, a building or structure shall be supplied by a maximum of _____ feeder(s) or branch circuit(s), unless specifically permitted otherwise.
In accordance with Article 225—Outside Branch Circuits and Feeders, the disconnecting means for a building supplied by a feeder shall be installed at a(an) _____ location.
Service conductors shall be considered outside of a building or other structure where installed under not less than _____ of concrete beneath a building or other structure.
Circuit conductors other than service conductors, shall not be installed in the same _____ as the service conductors.
Where a service _____ enters a building or structure, it shall be sealed in accordance with 300.5(G) and 300.7(A).
The minimum point of attachment of overhead service conductors to a building shall not be less than _____ above finished grade.

Barriers shall be placed in service equipment such that no uninsulated, ungrounded service busbar or service _____ is exposed to inadvertent contact by persons or maintenance equipment while servicing load terminations with the service disconnect in the open position.
The service disconnecting means shall be marked to identify it as being suitable for use as service equipment and shall be _____.
All services supplying _____ shall be provided with a surge-protective device (SPD).

choices.b: guest rooms and suites of hotels and motels
choices.c: patient sleeping rooms in nursing homes and limited care facilities

questions.q: There shall be no more than _____ service disconnects installed for each service or for each set of service-entrance conductors as permitted in 230.2 and 230.40.
For one- and two-family dwelling unit service conductors, an emergency disconnecting means shall be installed in a readily accessible _____ location.

choices.b: largest overcurrent device protecting the circuit conductors

choices.c: equipment bonding jumper or grounded conductor jumper
choices.d: equipment bonding jumper and grounded conductor jumper
